description: Sentiment model bake-off on the Kaggle 'Sentiment Analysis for Financial News' corpus (Malo et al. 2014). All accuracy/F1 numbers are on the identical held-out test split: 483 rows, stratified, seed 42.

results.note: no gain: base already trained on this corpus
newer architecture, no gain on this corpus

results.model: Jev 1.13 (closed System One model, zero-shot via hosted API)
results.note: weak on positive class; not deployable keyless
weak financial-tone judgment; 10x slower on CPU

conclusion: FinBERT base wins the bake-off and ships as the core scorer. Five models evaluated on identical data; the two fine-tuned variants land within noise of the base, and both System One decision models trail by 12-16 points. Evaluation artifacts: kaggle/ kernels, data/cache/sentiment_eval_*.json, docs/evidence/laya_spike.json, docs/evidence/jev_spike.json.
caveat: Differences among the top three are within noise (483 rows, stderr ~1.4pp); the System One gap is real and large.
